messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
• 55 mph on rural interstates,
• 45 mph on urban interstates,
• 35 mph on rural highways,
• 25 mph on urban highways.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 15 mph if posted). | Speed limits are enforced by both radar and speed cameras. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine plus points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%). | Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Stop signs: all vehicles must stop and yield to those already stopped.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to traffic citations. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied or the driver is overtaking a slow vehicle. | Improper lane changes can result in a fine. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is less than 200 ft. | Failure to use headlights when required can lead to a fine. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited.
• Disabled parking requires a valid disabled placard. | Violations can result in towing and fines. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red light: stop.
• Yellow light: stop if safe; otherwise proceed with caution.
• Green light: proceed. | Running a red light is a traffic violation with a $100 fine. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• In Texas, stopping is required in both directions. | Failure to stop can result in a $200 fine. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • All vehicles must have a working brake system, turn signals, and a valid registration.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in). | Non‑compliance can lead to a vehicle inspection ticket. | | **Points System** | • Traffic violations accrue points on the driver’s record.
• 12 points in 12 months can lead to license suspension. | Points are tracked by the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS). | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Driving without insurance can result in license suspension and fines. | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** website: [https://www.dps.texas.gov](https://www.dps.texas.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code** (available online) for detailed statutes. - Local city or county ordinances may impose additional rules (e.g., specific speed limits or parking restrictions). Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular traffic situation!
